name: St. Thérèse
bio:
Thérèse of Lisieux was born in 1873 in Alençon, France, the youngest of nine children. After her mother died when Thérèse was four, she grew up in Lisieux with her father and sisters, all of whom entered religious life. At fifteen she received special permission to enter the Carmelite convent at Lisieux, where two of her sisters already lived.

In the cloister she developed her 'little way' of spiritual childhood: doing small things with great love and trusting entirely in God's mercy rather than in heroic deeds. Obedient to her superiors, she wrote her autobiography, The Story of a Soul, which became a worldwide bestseller after her death from tuberculosis in 1897 at the age of twenty-four.

She was canonized in 1925 and declared a Doctor of the Church in 1997. Though she never left the cloister, she is co-patron of missions, having promised to spend her heaven doing good on earth.
